product.olivetti-m18p.summary: The Corona-derived transportable that took the M18 family beyond the office.
product.olivetti-m18p.history: The M18P was the transportable branch of the M18 range: Classic Tech identifies Corona Data Systems as the manufacturer and Docutel/Olivetti as the seller of the M18 P-1 alongside the desktop M18. An advertisement in COMPUTE!, June 1984, offered the M18-PT and M18 DT2; it establishes commercial availability, not a launch date. Professional use is documented in JVX report GM43855, dated October 1985: an M18P processed and archived geophysical survey data in Quebec using Scintrex Soft II.
product.olivetti-m18p.warning: Historical sheet under research: a BIOS with verified M18P provenance and the exact hardware revision are still missing.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.identity: The Corona origin is documented, but the model equivalence remains unresolved. MAME identifies the M18P with the PPC-21; The Retro Web lists it as a PPC-400 alias. Interchangeability between these revisions has not been established. The 1984 advertisement says “CALL”, without a numerical price.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.memory: RAM determined how much work the computer could load. TH99 attributes an 8088 and 128, 256, 384 and 512 KB populations to the M18P; this table still needs checking against an identified Olivetti board. The question mark in hardware flags this reservation.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.video: The integrated screen allowed the system to travel as a unit. An owner account describes a green CRT. TH99 lists a “VGA” port, an uncorroborated detail that is not adopted as the graphics standard; resolution and video logic remain unresolved.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.storage: The computer could collect and preserve field measurements. Report GM43855, p. 3, describes transfer over a serial link from a Scintrex IPR-11 and storage on floppy disk, with an Epson FX-80 printer. It does not identify the controller or disk format.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.firmware: The BIOS needed to boot still lacks a verified Olivetti identity. MAME mentions an M18P version 3.06 without providing a dump identified as such. ROMs for the Corona candidates do not establish compatibility with this computer.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.verified: Period advertising, a usage report and preserved technical attributions have been cross-checked. The reviewed BluMach has no M18P platform. MAME fc81fbe1 marks both coppc21 and coppc400 as not working; this is external project status, not a test performed here.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.limitati: The sheet cannot create or boot an M18P. Firmware with provenance, a technical manual and board photographs are needed to resolve the revision and its controllers. A machine image with clear publication rights is also pending.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_a: COMPUTE!, June 1984, BSD Enterprises advertisement, PDF page 157: M18 DT2 and M18-PT, both with prices on enquiry. Original preserved from Color Computer Archive.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_r: JVX Limited, MOP-2 IP/resistivity survey report, October 1985, GM43855, p. 3 (PDF page 9): M18P, Soft II and data workflow. Preserved from Quebec’s EXAMINE collection.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_o: Classic Tech, “Corona Data Systems (Westlake Village, Calif.)”: OEM relationship and M18/M18 P-1 names. A retrospective source; its Corona specifications are not automatically applied to the M18P.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_b: The Retro Web, “Corona Data Systems PPC-400”: lists Olivetti M18P as an alias. This attribution is retained alongside the conflicting one in MAME source.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_t: TH99, “Olivetti M18P”: CPU, RAM table and board jumpers. The revision identity and VGA reference need checking.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_m: MAME fc81fbe1, src/mame/pc/pc.cpp: PPC-21/M18P equivalence comment, ROM 3.06 reference and MACHINE_NOT_WORKING status of the Corona candidates.
product.olivetti-m18p.technical.source_o: Forum des VzEkC, “Mein neuestes Etwas”, post 2287, 24 September 2016: owner account of an M18P1 with a green screen and keyboard problems. No publication licence has been established for its photographs.
